title: Finite biproduct decomposition of the tensor source
statement: For a scheme X [def-pc-scheme], open U, cochain complexes P,F of module sheaves on U, and integers a,b,n, suppose P^r is zero for r<a or b<r. Put D=Hom(P,O_U[0]) [def-pc-ordinary-evaluation-data]. There is an isomorphism from the biproduct indexed by integers a<=r<=b of F^(r+n) tensor D^(-r) to degree n of Tot(F tensor D). Its composite with each biproduct inclusion is the total tensor inclusion for p=r+n and q=-r. No bound on F is assumed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08DQ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, last two displayed sums and the final finite-free/direct-summand evaluation calculation; Tag 08DM, lemma-Rhom-strictly-perfect, finite sum versus product calculation

proof.text: Use the Hom product projections to identify D^q with Hom(P^(-q),O_U), since every other target term of O_U[0] is zero. It follows that D^q is zero outside [-b,-a].

In the total tensor coproduct discard the zero summands, reindex by r=-q with p=r+n, and identify the finite coproduct with its biproduct. The inclusion equations characterize the resulting isomorphism. For an empty interval both source and target are zero.
